title: Development of an Improved Orthogonal Ribosome
abstract: A core goal of synthetic biology has been the evolution of macromolecular machines for compelling societal and scientific applications. Specifically, there has been significant interest in using directed evolution to engineer the ribosome for making new medicines and materials. Here we present our approach and progress in engineering the ribosome, which overcome previous hurdles in ribosome engineering. Integrating cutting­ edge computational RNA design of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) into the design­ build test cycle and using both in vivo and in vitro experimental platforms for ribosome synthesis and evolution, we modify and evolve the ribosome in ways previously intractable. Using our approach, we developed Ribo­T v3, a new and improved version of the tethered ribosome with an over 50% improvement in orthogonal protein translation. To evolve Ribo­ for improved function, we demonstrate the use of Rosetta­ guided design in iterative evolution experiments, and a new technique termed Evo­link (evolution and linkage of distant regions). Evo­link allows for the high-throughput evolution of functionally linked regions that are distal in primary sequence but close in 3D space by coupling flexible molecular biology techniques with next­-generation sequencing. Our work demonstrates the power of computational structural modeling for informing library design, and the potential of high­ throughput experimentation (Evo­link, cell­free ribosome assembly and translation) to optimize macromolecular machines for applications in energy, materials, and medicine.
